nodes.summary: Let $A, C$ be words over $\alpha$ and $B, D$ words over $\beta$, all viewed as words over the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$. If $AB = CD$ as words over $\alpha \oplus \beta$, then $A = C$ and $B = D$.

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a type of nonterminals, $u, v$ words over $\alpha \oplus \mathbb{N}$, $A, B \in N$, and $p, q$ strings of terminals in $\alpha \oplus \mathbb{N}$ and nonterminals in $N$. If $u\, A\, v = p\, B\, q$, where $u$ and $v$ are read as strings of terminals, then $p = u$, $B = A$ and $q = v$.

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality. Then $P$ has a PCP solution if and only if some word lies both in the language of the side grammar of $P$ for the top words and in the language of the side grammar of $P$ for the bottom words.

nodes.title: The side grammar of a PCP instance

nodes.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, let $\sigma$ assign a word over $\alpha$ to each domino, write $w_i = \sigma(d_i)$, and let $A$ be a nonterminal. The side productions are the list of encoded productions $A \to w_i \, A \, i$ and $A \to w_i \, i$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, k - 1$, where the letters of $w_i$ are terminals and $i$ is an index terminal.
nodes.title: The productions of a side grammar

nodes.title: The side word of an index sequence

nodes.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, set $d_i = (\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ for $i \ge k$, let $\sigma$ assign a word over $\alpha$ to each domino, and write $w_i = \sigma(d_i)$. For a nonterminal $A$ and a natural number $i$, this is the encoded production $A \to w_i \, i$, whose right-hand side is the letters of $w_i$ as terminals followed by the index terminal $i$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
